workflows.name: Get help on a command
workflows.goal: Open the documentation page for a ChimeraX command inside the built-in browser.
requests: how does the style command work?
show me the help page for color
whats the syntax for the volume cmd
workflows.notes: 'help <command>' opens that command's page. Typing a command name alone in the command line and clicking it in the Log also opens its help. Command names and keywords can be truncated to unique prefixes.

workflows.name: Open a tutorial web page inside ChimeraX
workflows.goal: Show an HTML tutorial in the ChimeraX browser so its cxcmd links execute commands when clicked.
requests: open this tutorial inside ChimeraX so I can click the commands
load a web page in the ChimeraX browser
open the chimerax mole tutorial page in chimerax
workflows.notes: Any http(s) URL of an HTML page opens in the ChimeraX Browser; cxcmd: links run when clicked. The built-in browser cannot download files. Menu Help / Tutorials lists the official ones.

workflows.name: Open a PDB entry and inspect chains, ligands and metadata
workflows.goal: Fetch a structure by PDB ID, see its chain/ligand tables in the Log, show a chain sequence and print citation/resolution metadata.
requests: Open 6n2y and tell me what chains and ligands it has
Fetch PDB 2hyy and show me what's in it
load 7kkj and whats its resolution
workflows.notes: The Log lists chains, non-standard residues and mmCIF assemblies; clicking a chain ID runs 'select /A', a ligand name 'select :ADP' (green outline). Ions like CL may be hidden until 'show :CL'. Hover an atom for chain/residue/atom name.

workflows.name: Close models or the whole session, clear the Log, quit
workflows.goal: Remove some or all models, reset the session, empty the Log, or exit ChimeraX.
requests: Close everything and start fresh
close model 2 only
clear the log and quit chimerax
workflows.notes: 'close' alone closes all models but keeps tools; 'close session' also closes tools such as the Sequence Viewer. Background and silhouettes are not reset by close (see publication look). No confirmation is asked; save a .cxs session first if needed.

workflows.name: Show, hide and close models by number
workflows.goal: Control which open models are displayed and remove models no longer needed.
requests: Hide model 3 but keep it open
Close models 2 through 4
show model 1 again pls
workflows.notes: '#2-4' is a range, '#2,3' a list. 'hide #3 model' hides the whole model (not just atoms). Same as the Model Panel eye checkboxes and close button. '#!1' means model 1 but not its submodels.

workflows.name: Set the working folder
workflows.goal: Choose the directory used for later open/save commands so no full paths are needed.
requests: Set my working directory to my project folder
let me pick a folder so I dont have to type paths
change the working folder
workflows.notes: Opens a folder chooser; menu equivalent File / Set Working Folder. Afterwards 'save domains.png' writes into that folder.

workflows.name: Run a ChimeraX command script (.cxc)
workflows.goal: Execute commands stored one per line in a plain-text .cxc file.
requests: run my command file
execute the commands in gbpmovie.cxc
open a cxc script
workflows.notes: Opening a .cxc runs its lines in order, like typing them separated by semicolons. Every GUI action echoes its command in the Log, so scripts can be built by copying from the Log. 'runscript file.cxc arg1 arg2' passes $1,$2 arguments.

workflows.name: Save a session
workflows.goal: Save the whole state (models, colors, named selections, views) to a .cxs file, then close models.
requests: Save my session
save everything as a cxs file
close all models after saving
workflows.notes: ChimeraX does not auto-save and asks no confirmation when closing. 'c' is short for cartoon. Reopen with 'open file.cxs'. In Preferences > Window tick 'Resize graphics window on session restore' for consistent figure sizes.

workflows.name: Startup aliases and tools for long commands
workflows.goal: Define aliases (or syntax reminders via echo) and startup tools in Preferences > Startup.
requests: Make a shortcut for a long command I use all the time
Show all my aliases
how do i make an alias in chimerax
commands: alias my_abbreviation mutationscores define avg fromScore amiss setAttribute true combine mean mutationSet #1
alias my_abbreviation echo "mutationscores define avg fromScore amiss setAttribute true combine mean mutationSet #1"
workflows.notes: Paste alias lines into 'Execute these commands at startup' (Preferences > Startup). The echo variant only prints the text. CliX (Toolshed) adds autocompletion. 'ks ri' selects residues between a clicked and ctrl-clicked residue.

workflows.name: Reusable script with arguments (AlphaMissense mapping)
workflows.goal: Save a workflow as a .cxc script taking $1/$2 arguments and call it through an alias.
requests: Make a script I can rerun for any UniProt ID
Automate the missense coloring for a given chain
script that takes arguments in chimerax
commands: mutationscores define avg fromScore amiss setAttribute true combine mean mutationSet $1
color byattribute r:avg $2 target csab palette bluered range full
workflows.notes: Lines 1-7 are the contents of map_missense.cxc; $1/$2 are replaced by arguments given after the script name. 'mutationSet $1' is needed when the script runs several times in one session. Put the alias line in Preferences > Startup; adjust the path.

workflows.name: Create a custom display preset script
workflows.goal: Save a .cxc style script in the presets folder so it appears in the Presets menu and can be applied by command.
requests: Set up my own default style preset
make a preset with round helices, silhouettes and white bg
apply my custom preset
workflows.notes: Lines 1-22 are an example my_custom_style.cxc. Set the presets folder in Preferences > Startup; scripts there show up in the Presets menu, or run 'preset my_custom_style'. Preset names can be truncated.

workflows.name: Split a multichain structure into one model per chain
workflows.goal: Separate chains into submodels so they can be compared or superimposed individually.
requests: Split 1t2p into separate models by chain
make each chain of model 1 its own model
split the chains up
workflows.notes: Result: #1.1, #1.2, #1.3 for chains A, B, C. Splitting dissociates chains from Sequence Viewer sequences; run 'seq assoc #1.2' before tools like Model Loops.

workflows.name: Duplicate a model and rainbow-color the copy
workflows.goal: Copy a model to apply a different coloring (N-to-C rainbow), then discard it.
requests: Make a copy of model 1 colored rainbow from N to C
duplicate my structure so I can color it differently
close the copied model
workflows.notes: 'combine' with one model makes a copy as a new model; check the Log/Models panel for its number before rainbow/close. 'rainbow' goes blue (N-term) to red (C-term); 'rainbow #3 structures' colors per copy, 'rainbow polymer palette BuPu' per chain.

workflows.name: Save, restore and zoom views
workflows.goal: Store the current orientation under a name, return to it later, and zoom to everything or to a selection.
requests: Remember this camera view so I can come back to it
Zoom to fit everything in the window
focus the view on my selection
workflows.notes: 'view' alone fits all models (toolbar icon runs 'view cofr false'). 'view <spec>' zooms onto it; 'clip false' turns off near/far clipping. Named views live in the session; 'view matrix' prints camera/model matrices to reuse elsewhere. 'view initial #2' restores a model's initial view.

workflows.name: Move the view: rotate, translate, zoom, center of rotation
workflows.goal: Reposition the view by command and pivot rotations around a ligand.
requests: rotate it 45 degrees around y and zoom in
center the view on the ligand and rotate around it
turn the molecule a bit
workflows.notes: Mouse: left-drag rotates, middle/right-drag (or Alt/Cmd+drag) translates, scroll zooms. 'cofr ligand' sets the center of rotation; 'ligand' is a built-in specifier. 'mousemode' alone lists current button assignments.

workflows.name: Atom specification basics (model/chain/residue/atom)
workflows.goal: Refer to parts of a structure with hierarchical specifiers and logical combinations.
requests: Select residues 45 to 55 in chain A of model 3
select all lysines in chain B
how do I say everything except nucleic acid
workflows.notes: Levels: # model, / chain, : residue, @ atom; omitted levels mean all. ',' = OR, '&' = AND, '~' = NOT, '|' = OR between groups. Built-ins: protein, nucleic, ligand, solvent, helix, strand, elements (C, N...). Most commands take specs directly (color #1/A red). Element symbols must be capitalized.

workflows.name: Select by distance (zones)
workflows.goal: Select atoms or whole residues within a cutoff of a reference set.
requests: Select residues within 5 Angstroms of the ligand
select everything within 8 A of model 1.2 as whole residues
select the stuff around residue 50 incl residue 50
workflows.notes: Syntax: select zone ref cutoff [other-spec] [extend t/f] [residues t/f]. 'residues true' selects whole residues; 'extend true' includes the reference. The ':<5.5' shorthand (residue level) and '@<6.3' (atom level) work in any spec, e.g. 'show ligand :< 5'.

workflows.name: Create and manage named selections
workflows.goal: Give reusable names to specs (dynamic) or to the current selection (frozen); list or delete them.
requests: Name residues 34-64 of chain A 'tm1' and color it
save the pocket around the ligand as a named selection
list my named selections
workflows.notes: Dynamic names re-evaluate the spec (also for models opened later); frozen names refer only to items present when defined. 'name delete <name>' removes one. Names are saved in sessions; define them in Startup preferences to have them always. '~select' deselects.

workflows.name: Define a named residue set and highlight it
workflows.goal: Name a set of residues (e.g. drug-resistance mutation sites), show them as gold balls, label and zoom to them.
requests: Highlight residues 250, 253, 256, 315 and 351 as gold balls
name a set of residues so I can refer to them later
show these mutation sites and zoom in on them
commands: color resist & C gold target al
workflows.notes: 'target al' colors atoms and labels only, leaving ribbons unchanged. 'view resist clip false' zooms to the set and turns off clipping. 'label height 1.0' sets 3D label height in Angstroms. 'seq chain /A' then 'select resist' shows them as green boxes in the Sequence Viewer.

workflows.name: Select an atom and expand or narrow the selection
workflows.goal: Select an atom by specifier, broaden to residue/secondary structure/chain, act only on the selection, then clear.
requests: select the NZ atom of Lys 43 then expand to the whole residue
how do I grow my selection to the whole chain?
clear the selection
workflows.notes: Ctrl-click an atom selects it; shift-ctrl-click adds; up-arrow ('select up') broadens atom -> residue -> secondary structure -> chain, down-arrow narrows. Toolbar buttons act only on the selection when one exists. Ctrl-click empty space or 'select clear' clears. 'sel' refers to the selection in any command.

workflows.name: Select the same residue on many chains with a wildcard
workflows.goal: Select one residue number on all chains matching a pattern and show them as colored spheres.
requests: Show Glu56 on all the c chains as red spheres
select residue 56 in every c subunit
highlight residue 56 accross all chains starting with c
workflows.notes: '/c*' matches chain IDs starting with c (c0..c9 in 6n2y). ':56' without a chain applies to every chain. Chain IDs are matched case-insensitively unless both cases exist.

workflows.name: Find and label truncated residues (missing atoms)
workflows.goal: Select residues whose atoms do not match their template (truncated sidechains) and label them.
requests: Which residues have missing side chain atoms?
label residues with incomplete coordinates
find truncated sidechains
workflows.notes: 'template-mismatch' is a built-in specifier for residues with missing/extra atoms. The Log reports the count. Missing atoms can affect MLP/ESP; repair with 'dockprep #1'.

workflows.name: Show a chain's sequence in the Sequence Viewer
workflows.goal: Open the sequence of a chain and select residues, which are highlighted in 3D and as green boxes in the sequence.
requests: open the sequence viewer for chain B and show whats missing
select residues 62 to 65 of chain A
pull up chain A in the sequence panel
workflows.notes: Light blue boxes mark beta strands, yellow helices; black-outlined boxes are residues missing from the structure. Click-drag in the sequence selects residues in 3D and vice versa. Hover a residue for its number. Clicking a chain name in the Log chain table does the same.

workflows.name: Show sidechains of regions that differ after superposition
workflows.goal: Starting from the matched core selected in the sequence alignment, invert the selection and display sidechains of the differing parts.
requests: Show the side chains of the regions that don't superimpose well
invert the selection and display the selected protein atoms
highlight the loop thats different between the two structures
workflows.notes: First click any light orange box in the Matchmaker sequence alignment to select the residues used in the final fit. 'select ~sel' inverts; 'disp' is a truncation of 'display', an alias of 'show'. Hover one-letter codes in the alignment to see residue numbers.

workflows.name: Select the narrowest part of a channel and show lining residues
workflows.goal: Select MOLE channel spheres below a radius cutoff and display protein residues near them.
requests: Which residues line the narrowest part of the pore?
select channel spheres with radius under 2 A and show residues within 2.5 A
show the constriction of the channel
workflows.notes: '@@radius<2' tests the atom attribute radius of the MOLE dummy atoms (model #2); ':<2.5' expands to whole residues within 2.5 A. For 1bl8 this shows Val 76/Gly 77 (selectivity filter). Backbone atoms stay hidden under cartoon unless 'cartoon suppressBackbone false'.

workflows.name: Standard colorings: by chain, heteroatom, rainbow, original look
workflows.goal: Apply common colorings and reset to the appearance at opening.
requests: Color each chain differently
color by element but keep the carbon colors
rainbow the ribbon N to C and then put it back how it was
workflows.notes: byhetero makes O red, N blue, leaves carbons. Rainbow goes blue (N-term) to red (C-term), best with ribbons. 'preset original' (menu Presets / Original Look) restores colors, styles and shown atoms. 'color list' prints all named colors.

workflows.name: Change atom display style (stick, ball, sphere)
workflows.goal: Set stick, ball-and-stick or sphere style for all atoms, one chain, a ligand or solvent.
requests: Show chain B as sticks
show the ligand as spheres
make the waters big red balls
workflows.notes: 'style' with no spec applies to all atoms. Residue names are case-insensitive (:sti works). 'preset sticks' shows all atoms as sticks. Waters are balls by default; 'solvent' is a built-in specifier.

workflows.name: Cartoon versus atom display, for all or one chain
workflows.goal: Switch between ribbon and atom representations, for the whole structure or single chains.
requests: Show the protein as ribbons only
hide chain C atoms and show its ribbon
show only chain A ribbon and nothing else
workflows.notes: 'hide' with no arguments hides atoms. 'ribbon /c' = 'show /c cartoon'. The 'only' keyword hides that type for everything else. Ligands become invisible after 'hide atoms'; show them with 'show ligand'. Toolbar Molecule Display buttons do the same.

workflows.name: Apply display presets
workflows.goal: Switch the whole scene to a built-in look: sticks, cylinders, ribbons, licorice, original look.
requests: Show the helices as cylinders
apply the sticks preset then go back to ribbons
reset to how it looked when i opened it
workflows.notes: Equivalent to the Presets menu. Names can be truncated and are case-insensitive (preset orig, preset pub, preset inter). Presets restyle the whole scene, so re-apply custom styling afterwards; newly opened structures get the default style.

workflows.name: Show, color, hide and close a molecular surface
workflows.goal: Display the solvent-excluded surface, color it like the atoms, hide parts, or delete it.
requests: show the surface of the structure
make the surface match the atom colors
get rid of the surface
workflows.notes: One surface per chain; waters/ligands are excluded. Clear any selection first or 'surface' acts only on selected atoms. 'color fromatoms' copies atom colors onto the surface. 'surface hide' hides, 'surface close' deletes. Surfaces are submodels (#1.1...).

workflows.name: Show only the surface around a ligand pocket
workflows.goal: Restrict the surface to the neighborhood of a ligand, keep the largest patch, and view ligand-pocket complementarity.
requests: Only show the surface within 8 A of the ligand
how well does the drug fill its pocket? show it as spheres in a transparent pocket
trim the surface to the binding site
workflows.notes: 'max 1' / 'visiblePatches 1' keep only the largest connected piece. 'target ar' hides atoms and ribbons but not surfaces. 'surface :EJ4 :< 4' computes the surface only for residues within 4 A of the ligand. 'transparency 50' applies to displayed surfaces.

workflows.name: Clip a surface to reveal an interior pocket
workflows.goal: Enable a clipping plane that cuts the surface but not the atoms, so a buried ligand becomes visible.
requests: Cut the surface open so I can see the ligand inside
clip the surface but keep the ligand atoms unclipped
show the buried pocket in 1g74
workflows.notes: 'clip' enables near/far planes through the center. '#!1' is model 1 without submodels, so the atoms are unclipped while the surface (#1.1) stays clipped; the cap is submodel #1.1.1. Drag planes with the clip mouse mode (Right Mouse toolbar). 'clip off' disables.

workflows.name: Color a clipped surface and its cap by MLP or electrostatics
workflows.goal: Color the outer surface and the planar clip cap by lipophilicity or Coulombic potential and make the cap semi-transparent.
requests: Color the cut surface and the cap by hydrophobicity
the cap isnt colored, color it by electrostatics too
make the clip cap 30% transparent
workflows.notes: The cap (#1.1.1) is not colored with the outer surface; name it explicitly. 'offset 0' evaluates the potential on the cap plane instead of 1.4 A outward. Coulombic palette: red -10, white 0, blue +10 kcal/(mol e); MLP: cyan hydrophilic to goldenrod lipophilic.

workflows.name: Style DNA as a smooth tube with nucleotide stubs
workflows.goal: Draw nucleic acid backbones as uniform round tubes with short base stubs.
requests: Make the DNA a tan tube
show the DNA backbone as a round cartoon with base stubs
simplify the nucleic acid display
commands: cartoon style nucleic xsection round width 1.5 thick 1.5
workflows.notes: Equal width/thickness with a round cross-section gives a tube. 'nuc stubs' replaces base atoms with stubs; 'nucleotides atoms' shows atoms, 'nucleotides fill' filled bases.

workflows.name: Highlight a ligand: color carbons, heteroatoms, thicker sticks
workflows.goal: Make a bound ligand stand out by coloring its carbons, keeping element colors for N/O/S, and fattening its sticks.
requests: Color the imatinib carbons salmon
make the ligand orange but keep oxygens red and nitrogens blue
make the ligand sticks fatter
workflows.notes: Element symbols must be capitalized (C). 'color byhet' recolors non-carbons by element and leaves carbons, so run it after the ligand color. Default stick radius is 0.2 A. 'select ligand' then 'color sel magenta' is the GUI-style route.

workflows.name: Show only the binding site around a ligand
workflows.goal: Center on the ligand and display only it and residues within a few Angstroms, hiding everything else.
requests: Zoom in on the ligand and hide the rest of the protein
show just the residues within 5 A of the ligand
display only the binding site atoms near EJ4
workflows.notes: ':< 5' means whole residues with any atom within 5 A. 'hide ~sel' hides only atoms; ribbons need 'hide ribbon'. GUI: ctrl-click a ligand atom, press up-arrow to grow the selection, or menu Select / Residues / STI. 'clip off' removes clip planes.

workflows.name: Show a ligand with nearby residues of a superimposed model
workflows.goal: Hide one structure except its ligand, then show only residues of a second aligned structure within 5 A of that ligand.
requests: Show the drug from 2fwz with the 1ah8 residues around it
display only residues of the aligned model near the other model's ligand
hide glycerol and water
workflows.notes: '#4 & #1:H71 :< 5' = atoms of #4 within 5 A (residue level) of residue H71 in #1. '|' is OR. Requires the models to be superimposed first (mm #4 to #1).

workflows.name: Change cartoon thickness
workflows.goal: Make ribbons thin tubes for an uncluttered fold view, or fat so coils are visible, then revert.
requests: Make the cartoon thinner
thicker ribbons so the loops are visible
go back to default ribbon style
workflows.notes: Values are in Angstroms. Other cartoon style keywords: xsection (round/rect/oval), modeHelix tube, arrows. The preset restores defaults.

workflows.name: Show backbone atoms of residues drawn as cartoon
workflows.goal: Turn off the cartoon's suppression of backbone atoms so backbone N/O of displayed residues appear.
requests: Show the backbone atoms too, not just side chains
why are backbone atoms hidden when cartoon is on?
display backbone atoms along with the ribbon
workflows.notes: By default showing cartoon hides backbone atoms of that residue. Needed e.g. to see backbone H-bond donors/acceptors ('cartoon suppress false' is the same). Revert with 'cartoon suppressBackbone true'.

workflows.name: Hide or show atoms, cartoons and surfaces of a chain
workflows.goal: Remove one chain from view (all representations) to look inside, or hide just its cartoon.
requests: Hide chain A so I can see the pore inside
hide the nanobody cartoon
hide the ribbons of chains A B C
workflows.notes: 'targ acs' = atoms, cartoons, surfaces in one command; 'hide /A' alone hides only atoms. 'hide /A model' would hide the whole model instead.

workflows.name: Make ribbons, surfaces or maps transparent
workflows.goal: Set percent transparency on cartoons, surfaces or map surfaces to see overlaid models.
requests: Make chain B see-through
set the map 30 percent transparent
make chain B opaque again
workflows.notes: Number is percent (0 opaque, 100 invisible). 'target r' ribbons, 'c' cartoons, 'a' atoms, 's' surfaces; default is surfaces. For maps 'volume #1 transparency 0.5' uses a 0-1 fraction; the Map toolbar Transparent button is equivalent.

workflows.name: Switch to orthographic projection
workflows.goal: Turn off perspective so distant objects are not drawn smaller.
requests: Switch to orthographic view
turn off perspective
use ortho camera
workflows.notes: 'camera mono' returns to perspective projection. Useful for measuring-style figures and 2D-like views.

workflows.name: Publication look: background color and silhouettes
workflows.goal: Set a white (or other) background with black outlines for figures, or revert to the interactive black look.
requests: give me a white background with black outlines
make the background light cyan and add outlines
go back to the black background
workflows.notes: 'preset pub' = white background + silhouettes (menu Presets / Publication 1). 'graphics silhouettes depthJump' controls how much depth change draws an outline (smaller = more lines). 'preset interactive' restores black background without silhouettes. 'close' does not reset these.

workflows.name: Save an image
workflows.goal: Write a PNG of the current view, optionally larger, supersampled or with transparent background.
requests: save a picture of this view to my desktop
save a 1000 pixel wide image with transparent background
export a high res png of this
commands: save missense_worms.png supersample 4 tr true pixelSize 0.1
workflows.notes: Extension picks the format (.png/.jpg). Without a directory the file goes to the working folder. 'tr' abbreviates transparentBackground. 'windowsize' fixes the graphics size so labels/keys land consistently. Toolbar Snapshot saves at screen size.

workflows.name: Lighting presets: simple, soft, full, flat
workflows.goal: Choose lighting for speed (simple) or quality (soft ambient occlusion, full with shadows, flat).
requests: Turn on soft lighting with shadows
use simpler lighting, its slow
make the shading less smudgy
workflows.notes: soft = shadows from 64 directions approximating ambient occlusion (pockets visible); full adds a directional shadow; simple/default are fastest for morph playback and clip dragging. multishadow up to 1024 gives smoother gradations but slows rendering. Home toolbar has Lighting buttons.

workflows.name: Play through coordinate sets or models with a slider
workflows.goal: Step through NMR ensemble conformers, trajectory frames or a set of models.
requests: Show a slider to play through the NMR models
step through the 10 conformers of 8r4w
slider to compare my alphafold models
workflows.notes: NMR ensembles open as one model with several coordinate sets; the slider steps or plays them. For several separate models (#3-7) the slider shows one at a time. 'coordset #1 1,21' plays frames by command.

workflows.name: Clip planes: slab view, mouse mode, Side View
workflows.goal: Look at a thin slab of map and model using near/far clip planes, drag them with the mouse, and turn clipping off.
requests: Clip the view to a 10 A slab
let me drag the clip planes with the mouse
turn clipping off
workflows.notes: Offsets are relative to the center of rotation. Side View (Tools / General) shows planes as draggable lines. With clip on the right button, right-drag moves the near plane; shift-drag moves near and far together (Mac: cmd-drag). Simple lighting speeds up dragging.

workflows.name: Clip a surface with an explicit plane position and axis
workflows.goal: Cut open a molecular surface with front/back planes placed by coordinates to expose internal channels.
requests: Show the surface and cut it open so I can see the proton channel
set up front and back clip planes through the membrane region
clip perpendicular to the symmetry axis
workflows.notes: Positions/axes are specific to 6n2y; 'coord #1' means model #1 coordinates. In clip mouse mode hold alt to move the back plane. Use simple lighting while dragging, then soft lighting for a darker, legible cavity.

workflows.name: Label residues and adjust label size
workflows.goal: Add 3D residue labels, set their height or background, and remove them.
requests: Label the residues of chain A and make the labels bigger
label all residues whose atoms are visible
remove all the labels
workflows.notes: Default label height 0.7 A; 'label height 1.5' resizes existing labels. '@@display' labels residues with displayed atoms. 3D labels move with the structure; use 2D labels for publication captions. '~label ~interface' removes labels outside a named set.

workflows.name: Clean up selection, labels and pseudobonds, reset the view
workflows.goal: Clear the selection, delete labels, remove H-bond, clash and distance pseudobonds, and refit the view.
requests: Clear everything and reset the view
remove all labels and H-bond lines and zoom out
get rid of the hbonds and clashes
workflows.notes: '~command' deletes the pseudobonds that command created. 'view' with no arguments fits all displayed items. Several commands can go on one line separated by ';'.

workflows.name: Add a color key and 2D text labels to a figure
workflows.goal: Draw a color key matching a coloring plus captions, positioned by mouse or by fractional window coordinates.
requests: Add a color key for the electrostatic potential
put a legend and title on this figure
add a text label saying Conservation and move it bottom left
commands: key red:-10 white:0 blue:10 pos .51,.09 size .32,.04
workflows.notes: 'key true' on coulombic/mlp/color byattribute draws a key and opens the Color Key tool ('Adjust key with mouse'). Positions/sizes are fractions of the window; set 'windowsize' first. '2dlabels' without a name changes all 2D labels; the 'move label' mouse mode drags them. Compose the image before adding keys.

workflows.name: Color chains
workflows.goal: Color one or several chains with a named color, by spec or via selection.
requests: Color chain N teal
color chains B, E and F gold
make the two protofilaments different colours
workflows.notes: Chain specs use /ID with commas for several chains. Coloring applies to atoms, ribbons and surfaces unless 'target' limits it (e.g. 'target al'). Hover a ribbon to read the chain ID. 'color #3.2 lightblue' colors a submodel.

workflows.name: Highlight residues by number
workflows.goal: Color specific residues (e.g. mutation sites) to mark them, optionally on one model only.
requests: Color residue 166 orange and residues 21 and 50 lime
highlight residues 46, 50, 51 and 53 in yellow and label them
color residues 73 90 95 of model 2 red
workflows.notes: Residue lists are comma-separated without spaces. Specs without a model number apply to all open models and all chains. Add '& C' to recolor only carbons.

workflows.name: Color a surface by hydrophobicity (MLP)
workflows.goal: Compute molecular lipophilicity potential and color the protein surface to reveal hydrophobic pockets or membrane belts.
requests: where does this membrane protein sit in the bilayer?
show a lipophilicity surface with a color key
hydrophobic patches on the surface, please
workflows.notes: 'mlp' creates the surface if needed; palette dark cyan (hydrophilic) - white - dark goldenrod (lipophilic). Transmembrane proteins show a goldenrod belt. Same as the Molecule Display toolbar Hydrophobic button. Missing sidechain atoms slightly affect results.

workflows.name: Color a surface by Coulombic electrostatic potential
workflows.goal: Color protein surfaces by electrostatic potential computed on the fly, optionally only protein chains in a nucleic-acid complex.
requests: Show the electrostatic potential surface
color the protein by charge but leave the DNA as cartoon
electrostatic surface of chain A with a key
workflows.notes: No APBS needed; hydrogens are added internally. Red -10, white 0, blue +10 kcal/(mol e). 'coulombic protein' restricts surface creation and coloring to protein. 'from rcsb_bio' fetches the biological assembly directly. Toolbar Electrostatic button is equivalent.

workflows.name: Color by B-factor
workflows.goal: Color atoms/ribbons by B-factor to see flexible regions, with optional palette and range.
requests: Color the protein by B-factor
show which parts of the structure are most flexible
color by bfactor with a rainbow palette from 25 to 75 then undo
commands: color byattribute bfactor palette rainbow range 25,75
workflows.notes: Default blue (low) - white - red (high). In cryoEM entries the B-factor column may hold local-resolution-like values. Toolbar B-factor button is equivalent. Follow with 'color zone' to transfer colors onto a map.

workflows.name: Color residues by a custom attribute from a .defattr file
workflows.goal: Load per-residue values (e.g. NMR chemical shift perturbations) and color with a white-to-red palette.
requests: Color residues by chemical shift perturbation from my defattr file
map NMR chemical shift changes onto the structure
render by a custom attribute white to red
workflows.notes: 'r:csp' = residue attribute csp. Palette 'value,color:value,color' maps explicit values. GUI: Tools / Depiction / Render by Attribute. 'save file.defattr attrName avg' writes an attribute out.

workflows.name: Color a map to match nearby atoms
workflows.goal: Color the map surface by the colors of atoms within a distance, to show what the model explains (or B-factor on the map).
requests: Color the density that matches the model
which part of the map is not covered by the atomic model?
color the map by the bfactors of the atoms
workflows.notes: Make the map opaque first. Uncolored regions are density not accounted for by the model. Run 'color bfactor #1' first to effectively show B-factor on the map. Map toolbar 'Color near atoms' is equivalent. Blob coloring is lost when the level changes.

workflows.name: Color a structure by sequence conservation
workflows.goal: Open a multiple sequence alignment that associates with the structure and color residues by the seq_conservation attribute with palette, range, novalue color and key.
requests: Color my structure by conservation from this alignment
load the ConSurf alignment for 121p and color by conservation
conservation colouring cyan to maroon with a key
commands: color byattr seq_conservation palette cyanmaroon range -1.4,1.4
color byattr seq_conservation protein palette cyanmaroon range -1.4,1.4 novalue yellow
color byattr seq_conservation palette cyanmaroon range -2,3 novalue silver key true
workflows.notes: Auto-association shows as a colored box around the sequence name; the Log reports the value range. Residues in gappy columns, ligands and unassociated chains have no value (keep their color unless 'novalue'). 'protein' limits recoloring. Gap tolerance: right-click sequence > Settings > Headers.

workflows.name: Manually associate an alignment sequence with a chain
workflows.goal: Associate a structure chain with its best-matching sequence when auto-association fails, then color that chain by conservation.
requests: Associate chain R with the alignment
the alignment didnt link to my structure, connect it to chain R
color just the receptor chain by conservation
commands: color byattr seq_conservation /R & protein range -1.5,3 novalue gray
workflows.notes: No colored box around a sequence name means no association. GUI: right-click sequence > Structure > Associations. Red boxes mark mismatches, which do not prevent association. 'seq dissoc #2' / 'seq assoc #1.2' manage associations by model.

workflows.name: Show and label highly conserved residues; find residues without values
workflows.goal: Display and label residues above a conservation cutoff, and select residues lacking a conservation value.
requests: Show only residues with conservation above 1.8 and label them
which residues have no conservation value?
label the most conserved residues
workflows.notes: '::attr>value' is an attribute-based residue spec; '~::seq_conservation' selects residues without the attribute (gappy columns, ligands, unassociated chains). Raising the AL2CO gap fraction (Sequence Viewer Settings > Headers) gives more residues values.

workflows.name: Color a channel surface by radius
workflows.goal: Color a MOLE channel surface by the radius attribute of its spheres using a built-in or custom palette.
requests: Color the channel by its radius
show where the pore is narrow versus wide
color the MOLE surface with my own colors
workflows.notes: The surface must exist ('surf #2') since coloring applies to the surface, not the spheres. Custom palettes are colon-separated color names; ColorBrewer names (puor, BuPu...) work. Add 'key true' for a legend.

workflows.name: Color a channel surface by protein MLP or electrostatics
workflows.goal: Compute lipophilicity or Coulombic potential from the protein atoms and map it onto a separate channel surface.
requests: Color the pore surface by the protein's lipophilicity
show the charge inside the channel
map the protein's coulombic potential onto the MOLE surface
workflows.notes: First argument = atoms used for the calculation; 'surfaces #2' = surface to color. 'offset -1' samples inside the channel surface (default 1.4 A outward). Optionally repair sidechains first with 'dockprep #1'.

workflows.name: Style a large complex and color chains by description
workflows.goal: Apply a large-structure preset, name all copies of a protein via its chain description, and color chains, protein and nucleic acid distinctly.
requests: Give every chain a different color with a nice palette
color all copies of THOC4 yellow regardless of chain ID
show the RNA in black
workflows.notes: '//description=...' selects chains by their mmCIF description, avoiding chain-ID lookup and working across structures; the leading * handles fusion prefixes. Any ColorBrewer palette works with rainbow.

workflows.name: Measure buried surface area and SASA
workflows.goal: Compute the buried area between two chains or models and the total solvent-accessible area.
requests: how much surface area is buried between chains A and B?
calculate the SASA of the protein without waters
is this crystal contact a real interface? measure buried area between copies 4 and 7
workflows.notes: Results go to the Log (e.g. 2bbv: 1900 A^2 between /a and /b). Rule of thumb: biological interfaces bury > 500 A^2 per side. '& ~solvent' excludes waters. 'with' abbreviates withAtoms2.

workflows.name: Chain contact graph and interface residues
workflows.goal: Show which chains contact each other, then select, display, label and list residues at an interface.
requests: which chains are in contact with each other?
show the interface residues as ball and stick with hydrogen bonds
list the contact residues so I can design mutants
workflows.notes: 'interfaces' opens a plot of chains with buried areas; right-click a chain node for 'Select Contact Residues'. 'info residues ... saveFile path' writes the list. 'ALYs' is a named selection; replace with your chain spec.

workflows.name: Find hydrogen bonds involving a ligand
workflows.goal: Show H-bonds between a ligand and protein/water as dashed lines, reveal partner residues, list them, and remove them.
requests: Show hydrogen bonds between imatinib and the protein
which residues H-bond to the ligand?
find hbonds to the selected ligand and log them
commands: hbonds sel restrict cross reveal true log true
workflows.notes: 'reveal true' displays hidden atoms of partners; H-bond pseudobonds only show when both atoms are displayed. 'restrict cross' with sel keeps bonds with exactly one end selected. Structures without hydrogens use inferred positions. GUI: Tools / Structure Analysis / H-Bonds.

workflows.name: Hydrogen bonds between two chains or a selection and the rest
workflows.goal: Find H-bonds across an interface or from selected residues, label the partners, and relax the distance criterion for salt bridges.
requests: Show hydrogen bonds between the nanobody and the spike
find residues H-bonded to residues 217-232 and label them
show the salt bridge between D128 and the peptide
commands: hbonds sel restrict cross reveal true
hbonds sel reveal true restrict cross interModel false select true
workflows.notes: 'hbonds' alone can be crowded. 'interModel false' ignores other models; 'select true' replaces the selection with the H-bonded atoms so 'label sel' labels partners. 'distSlop 0.6' loosens the distance cutoff by 0.6 A. Results table appears in the Log.

workflows.name: Find contacts of a ligand and list contacting residues
workflows.goal: Identify residues in van der Waals contact with a ligand, display and label them, and list them without drawing pseudobonds.
requests: Which residues contact the ligand?
list the protein residues that touch the FPS ligand
find all contacts of the selected ligand
commands: contacts :sti makePseudobonds false reveal true log true
contacts sel restrict cross reveal t log t select t
workflows.notes: 'select t' selects contacting atoms; '~sel ~protein' then drops non-protein so 'info residues sel' lists protein residues. Log sorts by VDW overlap (positive = intersecting). GUI: Tools / Structure Analysis / Contacts.

workflows.name: Check clashes
workflows.goal: Count internal clashes of a model, or monitor clashes of one residue continuously while moving its sidechain.
requests: Check the loop models for clashes
how many self clashes does model 3.3 have?
live clash detection for Tyr 248 while I rotate it
commands: clashes sel restrict cross reveal t continuous t
workflows.notes: 'restrict' to the same model limits to self-clashes; 'make f' skips pseudobonds (count in Log/status). 'continuous t' updates as coordinates change (clashes in purple). GUI: 'tool show Clashes'.

workflows.name: Measure, set and interactively rotate torsion angles
workflows.goal: Report chi1/chi2 of a sidechain, set a torsion to an exact value, or rotate a bond with the mouse.
requests: What are the chi1 and chi2 angles of Tyr 248?
let me rotate the Tyr 248 sidechain with the mouse
put residue 248 back to its original chi angles
workflows.notes: Four atoms without a value just report the angle; adding a value sets it. 'mouse right bond' assigns bond rotation to the right button (right-drag on the CA-CB bond changes chi1). Combine with continuous clash checking.

workflows.name: Measure distances between atoms
workflows.goal: Display atom-atom distances as labeled dashed lines and remove them.
requests: Measure the distance between Ser 21 OG and O1B of residue 302
what is the spacing between layers in this fibril?
remove all distance measurements
workflows.notes: Atom spec is /chain:residue@atom. GUI: ctrl-click one atom, shift-ctrl-double-click the second, choose Distance; or the distance mouse mode. Fibril layer spacing in 6h6b is ~4.90 A.

workflows.name: Superimpose structures with Matchmaker
workflows.goal: Align one or more models onto a reference (whole models or specific chains), optionally showing the sequence alignment.
requests: Align 2zco onto 3w7f
superimpose chain A of model 1 onto chain F of model 2
overlay these structures and show the alignment
workflows.notes: 'mm' abbreviates matchmaker. Sequence alignment (residue type + secondary structure) then iterative CA fit; RMSD in Log. The 'to' model stays fixed. 'bring #3' moves another model (e.g. a map) along. Restrict to a rigid domain with a named selection for stable fits. GUI: Tools / Structure Analysis / Matchmaker.

workflows.name: Compare superimposed structures: tile, pick residues, report transformation
workflows.goal: Lay aligned models side by side, locate a differing residue, or align a copy with 'align' to report rotation and shift (e.g. fibril twist).
requests: show the two structures side by side
find where residue 41 differs between the two structures
what is the twist angle between the two protofilaments?
workflows.notes: 'tile' arranges models in a grid. 'align' fits exact atom pairs and with reportMatrix logs rotation angle and shift along axis (6h6b: 179.5 deg, 2.45 A = half a layer). Clicking a residue in the Matchmaker alignment selects it in 3D.

workflows.name: Show crystal packing with unit cells
workflows.goal: Generate symmetry copies filling unit cells, color each copy, and measure buried area between neighbors.
requests: Show the crystal packing for 7rfw
display two unit cells and color each copy differently
is this crystal contact biological?
workflows.notes: Copies become submodels of a new model (#3.1, #3.2...) plus an outline box. GUI: Tools / Higher-Order Structure / Unit Cell. 7rfw: 1857 A^2 for the real dimer vs 467 A^2 for a crystal contact. Close the copies before building the biological assembly.

workflows.name: Build a biological assembly
workflows.goal: List the mmCIF assemblies and build one as a new model or in place, or fetch it directly.
requests: what biological assemblies does this structure have?
generate the biological assembly for 2hyy and drop the asymmetric unit
show the pentamer of the capsid
commands: sym #1 assembly 3 newmodel false copies false
workflows.notes: 'sym #1' lists assemblies in the Log; clicking a number there runs 'sym #1 assembly N'. Default makes copies in a new model (#2 or next free); 'newmodel false copies false' transforms in place (reverse with 'close #2; show #1 model'). 'color #3.2 lightblue' colors one copy.

workflows.name: Delete chains, residues, solvent or hydrogens
workflows.goal: Remove parts of a structure: a redundant chain, a fusion domain, waters, everything except some chains.
requests: Delete chain B
remove the fusion domain residues 1002 to 1106
delete the waters and everything except chains I and G
workflows.notes: Deletion is permanent for the session (reopen to restore). 'end' means the last residue. Chain IDs are case-sensitive when both cases exist. Hide surfaces before deleting to avoid stale patches. Check the Log chain table first.

workflows.name: Add hydrogens or run dock prep
workflows.goal: Add hydrogens (optimizing H-bonding), or repair truncated sidechains and add charges with dockprep.
requests: Add hydrogens to the structure
protonate the model
repair the missing side chains and add hydrogens
workflows.notes: Experimental structures usually lack hydrogens. dockprep also adds charges and completes sidechains. 'hide H' hides hydrogens; 'delete H' removes them (e.g. before comparing to density).

workflows.name: BLAST a chain or region against the PDB
workflows.goal: Find related experimental structures by sequence and load hits superimposed on the query.
requests: Blast chain B against the PDB
find other structures similar to this helix
search the pdb for homologs of my selection
workflows.notes: Runs on a web server; the Blast Protein table lists hits (sort by column, NMR entries lack resolution). Double-click or select rows and 'Load Structures' to open hits matched onto the query. 'cterm' is a named selection. Cannot restrict by species.

workflows.name: Find structural homologs with Similar Structures (Foldseek) and copy their ligands
workflows.goal: Run a shape-based search, show and cluster backbone traces of hits, and transfer ligands from selected hits onto the query.
requests: Find structures similar in shape to my protein
run a foldseek search and show the hits
which drugs bind to homologs of this protein?
workflows.notes: GUI in the tool: Search, then Traces / Clusters buttons; sort by Species, select rows, tick 'for selected rows only' and press Ligands (copies land in a new model, e.g. #3). Hide waters, ions and sugars to find real ligands. Searches 200M AlphaFold models too.

workflows.name: Open an NMR ensemble with its distance restraints
workflows.goal: Load a multi-model NMR entry and overlay PDB distance restraints colored by whether they are satisfied.
requests: Show the NOE restraints for 8r4w
which NMR restraints are violated in this ensemble?
open 8jr6 with its nmr constraints
commands: hide cartoon ; show atoms ; nucleotides atoms
workflows.notes: Green = satisfied, yellow = too long in the current model. Most restraints involve hydrogens, so show plain atoms (not cartoon/slabs) to see them. 'structures #3' attaches restraints to a specific model. Needs the NMR-STAR reader (ChimeraX 1.7 daily or Toolshed).

workflows.name: Show UniProt annotations on a structure
workflows.goal: Associate UniProt sequence features with a chain so the Feature Viewer highlights annotated regions.
requests: Show the UniProt annotated domains on my model
map uniprot features onto chain A
open the feature viewer for this protein
workflows.notes: GUI: click the UniProt name in the Log chain table. Clicking a feature selects those residues. Works for any model, not only AlphaFold ones.

workflows.name: Open MOLEonline channel results as spheres or a surface
workflows.goal: Load a MOLE JSON results file so the channel appears as spheres, then surface it for coloring.
requests: Open my MOLE channel JSON file
show the pore computed by MOLE as a smooth surface
load MOLEonline results
workflows.notes: Generate the JSON on the MOLEonline site (Pore mode, Download > JSON). 'open browse' opens a file dialog; or give the path with 'format mole'. Spheres are dummy atoms with a radius attribute; 'surf #2' is required before mlp/coulombic/byattribute coloring.

workflows.name: Mutate a residue and choose rotamers
workflows.goal: Swap a residue for another amino acid with the best rotamer, or inspect rotamers interactively by H-bonds and clashes.
requests: Mutate residue 128 to asparagine
model the A53E mutation in chains I and G
show tyrosine rotamers for Tyr 248
workflows.notes: 'swapaa' picks the rotamer avoiding clashes / optimizing H-bonds; 'interactive' opens a table (Dunbrack library) with probabilities; add H-Bonds/Clashes columns and 'Use Chosen Rotamer'. Pick by interactions, not just probability. Residue names are 3-letter codes.

workflows.name: Model a missing loop with Modeller (Model Loops)
workflows.goal: Fill an internal missing segment by generating several Modeller loop conformations and comparing their scores.
requests: Model the missing loop in chain B with Modeller
fill in the gap in chain B of 1t2p
rerun loop modelling with more flexible residues
workflows.notes: Menu Tools / Sequence / Model Loops: number of models 3, 'internal missing structure', adjacent flexible residues 1-2, Modeller license key (free academic). Results open as #2.1-2.3; most negative zDOPE is best. Before rerunning, dissociate the new models and reassociate the original chain.

workflows.name: Fetch an AlphaFold Database model by UniProt ID
workflows.goal: Retrieve a precomputed AlphaFold prediction colored by confidence, optionally with its PAE plot.
requests: Fetch the AlphaFold model for O51E2_HUMAN
get the alphafold prediction for this uniprot entry with the PAE plot
open an alphafold structure of my protein
workflows.notes: Colored by pLDDT: blue high (>90), red low (<50, may be disordered). GUI: Tools / Structure Prediction / AlphaFold (Fetch; Predict runs ColabFold for mutated sequences, ~13 min). The PAE window can color by pLDDT or PAE domains.

workflows.name: Fetch AlphaFold models matching open chains
workflows.goal: Find the AlphaFold DB prediction for a chain's sequence and open it superimposed, optionally untrimmed and restyled like the experiment.
requests: Get the AlphaFold prediction for chain B and overlay it
show what parts of my crystal structure are missing using AlphaFold
alphafold match for chains A to D
workflows.notes: Matches by sequence (identity reported), superimposes and colors by pLDDT. 'trim false' keeps full-length predictions. 'mcopy' copies style/colors from one model to another. 'show true' opens the alignment. The DB lacks multimers.

workflows.name: Show the AlphaFold PAE plot and color by PAE domains
workflows.goal: Display predicted aligned error and color the model by rigid domains inferred from the PAE.
requests: Show the predicted aligned error plot
color the AlphaFold prediction by its PAE domains
which parts of this model are reliably packed together?
workflows.notes: AlphaFold is not confident about relative packing of different domains, so fit them into maps separately. Dragging in the PAE plot selects residues. 'file' attaches a local PAE JSON (AF3 output).

workflows.name: Fit an AlphaFold model into a cryoEM map
workflows.goal: Trim a prediction to one domain, smooth the map, place the model by hand, optimize the rigid fit and compare with the deposited structure.
requests: Fit the AlphaFold model into the density
dock the predicted structure into the EM map and refine
compare my fitted model with 8f76
workflows.notes: Map #2, AlphaFold #3, smoothed map #4. Hand placement: right-drag translates, shift-drag rotates the selected model; the view matrix line reproduces the tutorial's placement. 'delete #3:1-27,337-end' trims to a domain first when PAE shows separate domains. ISOLDE can refine further.

workflows.name: Load AlphaMissense scores and color/label by pathogenicity
workflows.goal: Fetch AlphaMissense predictions for a human protein, show substitution matrices, color and thicken the cartoon by mean score, and export values.
requests: Show AlphaMissense pathogenicity on my AlphaFold model
color the protein by average missense pathogenicity
make ribbon thickness reflect mutation sensitivity
commands: open Q86V81 fromDatabase alpha_missense format amiss
mutationscores label #1 amiss height 3 palette bluered
mutationscores define avg fromScore amiss setAttribute true combine mean
color byattribute r:avg #!1 palette bluered key true
workflows.notes: Human proteins only. Blue tolerated, red sensitive. High scores in disordered regions often mark binding motifs. Add 'mutationSet #1' when several score sets are loaded. Render by Attribute GUI is an alternative.

workflows.name: Analyze an AlphaFold 3 prediction folder for interfaces
workflows.goal: Read an AF3 output directory, summarize confident inter-chain contacts, open the best model with PAE and keep the interface selection.
requests: Look at my AlphaFold 3 prediction and show the interface
which of my AF3 models has the most confident contacts?
load the best alphafold multimer result
workflows.notes: Folder is the unpacked AF3 server zip; dimers only for now. Check the Log summary and click the link to open the PAE plot and best model. Interface residues are selected and contact lines drawn colored by PAE; name the selection before clicking elsewhere.

workflows.name: Compute AlphaFold inter-chain contacts colored by PAE
workflows.goal: Open an AF3 model, attach its PAE file, and draw or export predicted contacts between chains.
requests: Show the contacts between chain A and the other chains colored by PAE
write the predicted contacts to a text file
attach the pae json to my alphafold model
commands: alphafold contacts last-opened & /A toAtoms last-opened & /B distance 4.0 maxPae 5.0
workflows.notes: 'last-opened' refers to the most recently opened model (script-friendly); or 'open file id 1000'. One chain spec maps contacts to all others; no spec includes intra-chain. The last form is what 'alphafold interfaces' runs.

workflows.name: Tidy a close-up of a predicted interface
workflows.goal: Switch to a thin-cartoon preset, keep labels only on interface residues, show their atoms and focus the view.
requests: Clean up the view so only the interface residues are labeled
zoom in on the interface and color side chains by element
thinner cartoon for a close up
workflows.notes: 'interface' is a named selection. '~label ~interface' removes labels outside it. 'colour' is accepted for 'color'. '#!2' is model 2 without submodels.

workflows.name: Overlay multiple predictions, copy coloring and browse with a slider
workflows.goal: Open all AF3 models from a run, apply one model's coloring to the rest, align them on a rigid domain and step through them.
requests: Open all five AlphaFold models and align them
apply the same coloring to all my predictions
slider to compare the predicted conformations
workflows.notes: '*.cif' opens every CIF in the folder. A dynamic name matches the residues in every model. Aligning on a small rigid domain gives a stable superposition. Check the Log for assigned model numbers.

workflows.name: Open a cryoEM map from EMDB, alone or with its PDB model
workflows.goal: Fetch a density map by EMDB ID, optionally together with the atomic model built into it, and view them together.
requests: Open EMDB map 25428
open 8f76 and its cryoEM map
fetch emd 1080 and turn on shadows
workflows.notes: Both 'N from emdb' and 'emdb:N' work. The Log 'more info' link of a PDB entry gives its EMDB ID. Deposited models open already positioned in the map. Large maps (>100 MB) are slow to fetch; they open subsampled (step 2). Model numbers follow opening order.

workflows.name: Adjust map threshold, step, style, dust and transparency
workflows.goal: Set the contour level (by value, mouse or enclosed volume), show full resolution, switch to mesh, hide small blobs and make the map see-through.
requests: set the threshold to 0.9
my map looks blocky, show it at full resolution
hide the noise specks and make the map transparent
workflows.notes: 'vol' abbreviates volume; options combine in one command. Hover the map to read the level; drag the Volume Viewer histogram bar to change it. 'enclose' picks the level enclosing a volume in A^3. Map toolbar has Hide Dust, Transparent, Mesh buttons.

workflows.name: Place a model by hand and fit it into a map (rigid body)
workflows.goal: Move a model into the density with the mouse or by command, then locally optimize the fit.
requests: fit 1grl into the EMD-1080 map
let me drag the spike model into the EM map then refine
dock my model in the density
workflows.notes: 'fit' = fitmap; it is a LOCAL optimization so start from a rough manual placement. Move mode: ctrl-click an atom to select the model, right-drag translates, shift-drag rotates (Mac: option+trackpad). Map toolbar Fit button is equivalent. Correlation is reported in the Log.

workflows.name: Fit into a Gaussian-smoothed map for a larger convergence radius
workflows.goal: When fine detail traps the fit, smooth the map, fit into the smoothed copy, then discard it.
requests: The fit gets stuck, smooth the map and fit again
apply a gaussian filter to the density with width 3
blur the map so I can see the helices
workflows.notes: 'volume gaussian' makes a new map model (#4) and hides the original. GUI: Tools / Volume Data / Map Filter. Fitting does not resolve pseudo-symmetry; choose the correct symmetry-related placement manually.

workflows.name: Fit a second component into unexplained density
workflows.goal: Open another structure, strip extra copies and waters, place it by hand in density not covered by the first model, and fit.
requests: Fit the nanobody 7kkj into the EM map
delete chain C and the waters from model 3 then fit it
place a ligand structure into the leftover density
workflows.notes: Spike #1, map #2, nanobody #3. First 'color zone #2 near #1 distance 5' to see unexplained density. Ctrl-click an atom of #3, right-drag to move (shift to rotate), then fit once per placement. Orientation is hard; repeat for symmetry copies.

workflows.name: Simulate a map from a model and subtract it from the experimental map
workflows.goal: Create a simulated density from the fitted model, show it as mesh, and subtract to reveal unexplained density.
requests: make a simulated map from my model at 10 angstroms
subtract the model density from the experimental map
show the difference density after fitting
workflows.notes: molmap creates a new map (#3); vol subtract creates another (#4). 'minrms t' scales the subtracted map to minimize RMS difference. Numbers assume map #1 and structure #2.

workflows.name: Open an X-ray density map from the EDS with its model
workflows.goal: Fetch the crystallographic map for a PDB entry, show it as mesh, and extend it by symmetry to cover an assembly.
requests: open the electron density for 1a0m
show the x-ray map for 7rfw and cover the whole dimer
get the density from EDS as mesh
workflows.notes: Map opens before the model here, so map #1, model #2. 'volume cover' makes a NEW map using crystal symmetry, so later commands target it. Delete hydrogens ('delete H') before comparing. EDS server availability may change.

workflows.name: Show map density only near atoms or a ligand (zone)
workflows.goal: Restrict the displayed map to within a distance of atoms, tune level and transparency, and undo the zone.
requests: only show density within 2 angstroms of the atoms
zone the map around the ligand as a transparent mesh
remove the zone and show the whole map again
commands: volume zone #2 near :EJ4 range 6 newmap false
workflows.notes: 'volume zone' and 'surface zone' hide parts of the map surface, they do not crop data. Map toolbar Zone and Tools / Volume Data / Surface Zone are equivalent. Increase the distance to include neighboring side chains. Use 'volume #3 region i,j,k,i2,j2,k2' for a thin slab of planes.

workflows.name: Close-up of a helix with zoned mesh density and residue labels
workflows.goal: Show one residue range as sticks colored by element with the map zoned around it as transparent mesh and labeled residues.
requests: Zoom in on helix S4 residues 217-232 with density mesh and labels
show the density as a mesh around residues 8-19 of chain D only
how well does the map fit this helix?
workflows.notes: Model #1, map #4 here; 'hide ~sel ribbon' isolates a helix in a bigger complex. 'color byhet' keeps carbons tan. Restore with 'volume unzone ; volume style surface'.

workflows.name: Examine density around a ligand at different contour levels
workflows.goal: Center on a ligand, change the map threshold and mesh style to judge how well density supports it.
requests: Zoom in on the ADP and show me the density around it
is there density for the phosphate? lower the contour
check whether the ligand fits the map
workflows.notes: Level values are specific to EMDB 9333; adjust on the Volume Viewer histogram otherwise. Tentative ligands may only appear at lower levels. 'color byhetero' helps side-chain fitting.

workflows.name: Show a thin slab of a cryoEM map as mesh
workflows.goal: Restrict the displayed map to a range of grid planes and show it as mesh.
requests: Show just a thin slice of the map
crop the density to a few planes and show it as mesh
set the map threshold to 0.01 and use mesh style
workflows.notes: region is imin,jmin,kmin,imax,jmax,kmax in grid indices. Alternative: the crop mouse mode in the Right Mouse toolbar. 'volume #3 region all' restores everything.

workflows.name: Make a finer map mesh with triangle subdivision
workflows.goal: Subdivide mesh triangles for a smoother density mesh, then turn it off to keep rendering fast.
requests: Make the mesh smoother
subdivide the mesh triangles on the map
turn off the fine mesh its slow
workflows.notes: Subdivision multiplies triangle count; switch it off afterwards to avoid slow surface calculations.

workflows.name: Step through residues in density with Residue Fit
workflows.goal: Open the Residue Fit tool to view each residue in its map in sequence and optionally record it.
requests: check how well each residue fits the density
step through the residues in the map
record a movie of the residue fit
workflows.notes: Drag the slider or press play; the tool's record button writes resfit.mp4 to the Desktop and its stop button ends recording early. Structure #1, map #2.

workflows.name: Open a tomogram and browse it as slices or the full volume
workflows.goal: Load a large tomogram from EMDB, page through single planes, or show all planes with an outline box.
requests: Open the EMD-4191 tomogram and let me look through the slices
show the whole tomogram instead of one slice
open emdb 1273

workflows.goal: Take back everything the last request did, when the request opened, closed or otherwise changed more than a single command and plain undo cannot reach it.

tips.tip: This page is ChimeraX-only: it describes ChimeraX as the successor to Chimera, and none of its command syntax (e.g. /b chain specifiers, 'vol', 'sym ... assembly') should be assumed to work in legacy Chimera; a Chimera edition would need Chimera's own documentation as its source.
Use 'help <command>' (e.g. help style) to open the documentation for any command.
The command links on the page only execute when the page is shown in the ChimeraX internal browser (Help > Quick Start Guide in the ChimeraX menu).
Several commands can be entered on one line separated by semicolons (e.g. hide atoms; show ribbon).

Atom specifiers: /x = chain, :n = residue number, @name = atom name, #n = model; 'sel' refers to the current selection, 'solvent' and 'protein' are built-in categories, '&' intersects and '~' negates (e.g. #1 & ~solvent).
Selection with the mouse: ctrl-click an atom; shift-ctrl-click adds; ctrl-click the background clears; up-arrow and down-arrow keys expand and unexpand the selection (same as 'select up').

Mouse navigation: rotate by dragging, translate with the middle button or option-drag on Mac; the right-button function is set from the toolbar's Right Mouse tab (or the mousemode command); with a Mac one-button mouse, drag while pressing the command key.
Structures fetched from the PDB arrive in mmCIF format and are cached locally.
After 'sym #1' lists assemblies, do not click the links in the Log; if an assembly was generated by mistake, reverse it with 'close #2; show #1 model'.
Model numbers are sequential: opening a map first makes it #1, a structure #2, molmap output #3, vol subtract output #4; adjust commands if the order differs.
Hovering the mouse over a map reports its contour level in the status line.
Very large maps (e.g. a 200 MB tomogram) open as a single grayscale plane; use 'volume #1 region all' to show all planes and 'step 1' for full resolution.
'vol' abbreviates 'volume', 'transp' abbreviates 'transparency', and 't' means true (e.g. minrms t).
'light full' gives shadows; 'light default' is simpler lighting without shadows.
'close' with no arguments closes all models but does not reset background or silhouettes; use 'set bg black' and 'set silhouettes false' to restore defaults.
The toolbar video camera icon (command 'ks vd') records a spin movie saved on the Desktop as movie.mp4.
Capitalization of residue names in the command line is optional, but element symbols always need to be capitalized (e.g. ':sti & C').
Ctrl-click an atom then press the keyboard up arrow to promote the selection to the whole residue; if the initial pick is a bond rather than an atom, press up arrow twice.
Ctrl-click in empty space (or 'select clear') clears the selection.
Tables in the Log are clickable: chain IDs select chains, non-standard residue names select ligands, and mmCIF assembly numbers generate assemblies as new models.
Pseudobonds representing H-bonds or contacts are only displayed when both endpoint atoms are displayed, so use 'reveal true' to show the partner residues.
The structures have no explicit hydrogens; hbonds and coulombic use inferred hydrogen positions internally.
Ribbon display suppresses backbone atoms by default; use 'cartoon suppress false' to see backbone N and O atoms participating in H-bonds.
In 'surface zone', 'max 1' limits display to the largest surface component and hides disconnected bits.
'#!1' addresses model 1 itself but not its submodels, so 'clip model #!1 off' leaves the surface (#1.1) clipped while atoms are unclipped.
The planar cap of a clipped surface (submodel #1.1.1) is not automatically colored with the outer surface and needs its own mlp/coulombic command; use 'offset 0' for coulombic on the cap.
MLP coloring can differ from per-residue hydrophobicity lookup scales such as Kyte-Doolittle because all amino acids contain both polar and nonpolar atoms.
'coulombic protein' restricts surface creation and coloring to protein chains; hide protein atoms first so only surface, DNA and ligand remain.
When making a figure, compose the rest of the image before adding a color key or 2D labels.
With 'Adjust key with mouse' checked in the Color Key tool, mouse drags move the key instead of the structure; uncheck it to rotate again.
Selections appear as green boxes in the Sequence Viewer, and clicking or dragging in the sequence selects the corresponding residues in 3D.
'close' closes models only, while 'close session' also closes associated tools such as the Sequence Viewer.

Conservation values are only assigned to residues of structures associated with the alignment; solvent, ligands, ions and unassociated chains lack seq_conservation and are affected by the novalue option unless you restrict the spec (e.g. 'protein' or '/R & protein').

Alignment columns with a high proportion of gaps get no conservation value, so termini and loops may stay their original color; raise the Gap fraction in Sequence Viewer Settings > Headers to cover more residues.
The full range of conservation values is reported in the Log after 'color byattr'; use the range option to emphasize extremes, and values outside the range get the end colors of the palette.

Automatic sequence-structure association is indicated by a colored box around the sequence name; if none appears, associate manually with 'sequence associate' or the sequence window context menu Structure > Associations.
Small mismatches (red boxes in the alignment) between structure and alignment sequence do not prevent association.
3D labels move with the structure; use 2D labels for publication images.
'light soft multishadow 512' improves ambient shadows but a high number of directions can slow interactive manipulation.
Sizes and positions for the color key and 2D labels are window-relative, so appropriate values depend on the graphics window dimensions.

Changes in Sequence Viewer conservation settings apply immediately (histogram updates), but you must rerun 'color byattr seq_conservation' to recolor; Save stores settings as preferences, Reset restores factory defaults.
The default conservation measure is the AL2CO entropy-based method; variance-based and sum-of-pairs measures are also available in the Headers settings.

This page contains only ChimeraX commands, so an old-Chimera edition cannot be derived faithfully from it; the equivalent Chimera workflow uses different tools and syntax and would need a separate source.
Hydrogen atoms are usually omitted from experimental structures because they are too small to resolve; use addh to add them, and they are positioned to optimize hydrogen bonding.
Most hydrogen bonds with the ligand in 4n6h are to water molecules, so a ligand-restricted hbonds display may show few protein contacts.
Model numbers shift during the session: 4n6h is #1, the EDS density map is #2, after close #2 the 6pt2 structure becomes #2, and the morph trajectory is #3.
Mouse over chain ends in the graphics window to read residue numbers before deleting a crystallization fusion domain (1002-1106 in 4n6h, 999-1106 in 6pt2).
Clip planes are set in the GUI (Tools / General / Side View, drag the vertical lines) and must be removed with clip off before zoning or viewing the whole structure.
Density map contour level can be set by dragging the bar on the Volume Viewer histogram or with volume level.
A morph only includes atoms present in both structures, so ligands are not part of the morph.
Delete hydrogens (delete H) before comparing atoms to x-ray density so they do not clutter the view.
The most probable rotamer from swapaa is not necessarily the one that preserves a key hydrogen bond; check the interactive rotamer table.
Two intracellular alpha helices move about 10 Angstroms between the inactive (4n6h) and active (6pt2) delta opioid receptor states.

This page contains no old-Chimera (1.x) commands; an old-Chimera edition would have to be authored separately since several steps (mlp, light soft, open from eds, morph with same true, swapaa interactive) have no one-to-one Chimera command syntax on the page.
A Modeller license key is required to run Model Loops; academic users can obtain one free by registering at the Modeller website, and it is remembered in ChimeraX preferences.
Only 3 loop models are calculated in the tutorial for expediency; for most research purposes a higher number is recommended.
The longer the segment being modeled, the more likely some results are poor (over 50 percent poor predictions for segments of 10+ residues).
The best zDOPE score in the Modeller Results dialog is the most negative; choosing rows shows those models and hides the others.
Model Loops models every structure associated with the sequence, so dissociate new loop models (seq dissoc) and reassociate the original chain (seq assoc) before re-running.
Splitting a model with 'split' dissociates its chains from the Sequence Viewer, so reassociate the chain of interest afterwards.
Closing models in the Model Panel cannot be undone except by reopening or recalculating them.
Selection is shown with a bright green outline; clear it by Ctrl-clicking empty space.
Model Loops calculations take a minute or two to run.
The AlphaFold Database does not cover all of UniProt and does not include multimeric protein structures.
In a real research situation, search for related structures (e.g. with Blast) before modeling a missing segment.
The tutorial is written for ChimeraX only (Modeller v10.1, November 2021) and contains no legacy Chimera commands, so an old-Chimera edition cannot be derived faithfully from this page.
The tutorial targets ChimeraX 1.9; if opened inside ChimeraX via Help / Tutorials, the command links on the page can be clicked to run them directly.

Model numbers in the commands (#1, #2, #3, #4) reflect the order models were opened in the tutorial; after closing a model its number is reused, so check the Model Panel and adjust specifiers to your own session.
'mm' is an accepted abbreviation for 'matchmaker', and 'sel' refers to the current selection.
':< 5' is a residue-level zone specifier (whole residues within 5 Å); '~' means NOT, '&' means AND, '|' means OR in atom specifiers.
The Log panel's chain table and 'more info' links identify chains (e.g. antibodies, G-proteins, nanobodies) and give the EMDB map id or fetch command for a PDB entry.
Large EM maps may open subsampled; use 'volume #N step 1' to show full resolution, and raise the contour level or use Hide Dust to suppress noise.
Smooth a map (volume gaussian) before placing a model by hand so helices are clearly visible, then run 'fit' against the smoothed map.
AlphaFold models are colored by confidence: blue means high confidence; predicting a mutated sequence from scratch takes about 13 minutes.
About 2/3 of Foldseek hits can have under 10% sequence identity and would be missed by sequence searches; copying ligands from hits fetches the PDB entries (about 20 s, 5 s if cached).
Downloaded attribute files (.defattr) must be opened from their local path (the page uses ~/Downloads/...), and the attribute name is referenced as r:name in 'color byattribute'.
Toolbar buttons (Hydrophobic, Sphere, Hide Dust, Fit) and the Similar Structures panel are described on the page as GUI actions without stated command equivalents.
