The tutorial was written for ChimeraX 1.7 (January 2024); model numbers #1-#5 assume you follow the steps in order, including deleting the unit-cell copies and outline before generating the biological assembly.
If the tutorial is opened inside ChimeraX (menu Help / Tutorials), each command link can be clicked to run it.
Clear the selection before running 'surface' or 'color' without a target, otherwise they act only on the selected atoms.
Buried surface area above about 500 A**2 is typical of biological interfaces; smaller contacts are usually crystal packing.
'volume cover' and 'volume gaussian' create new map models with new numbers; subsequent volume, zone and fit commands must target the new model, not the original.
'surface zone' only hides parts of the map surface near chosen atoms; it does not crop or change the map data.
Large cryoEM maps open at step 2; use 'volume #N step 1' for full resolution.
Noise in a cryoEM map can be removed either by raising the contour level or by keeping the recommended level and using Hide Dust (surface dust) with a size in Angstroms.
AlphaFold models are colored by pLDDT confidence; blue means high confidence.
'fit' (fitmap) is a local optimization, so hand-place the model in the density first, ideally in a Gaussian-smoothed map where helices are clear.
Fetching PDB NMR distance constraints ('open ID from pdb_nmr') requires the NMR-STAR file reader, available in daily builds from Jan 9 2024 or via Tools / More Tools on ChimeraX 1.7.
NMR distance constraints to hydrogens are only drawn when the hydrogen atoms are displayed, so hide cartoon and show atoms (nucleotides atoms) to see them.
Clip-plane mouse modifiers are given for Mac only (cmd-drag moves the front plane, shift-cmd-drag moves both planes).

The page contains no legacy Chimera (1.x) command syntax at all, so a faithful old-Chimera edition cannot be derived from this source; several commands (matchmaker, measure buriedArea, volume level/step, clip, sym) have Chimera namesakes with different syntax, which would need a Chimera-specific source.
The tutorial requires ChimeraX 1.5 or newer; the MOLE JSON reader (format mole) is not available in older versions.
The channel must be surfaced (surf #2) before mlp or coulombic with the surfaces option will color it; the spheres themselves are never colored.
For coloring a channel interior by ESP use a negative offset (offset -1); the default positive offset (1.4 A) is for the outside of a protein surface.
MOLE spheres are dummy atoms; their size is stored in the atom attribute radius, so use @@radius<2 in specifiers and color byattribute radius.
Showing cartoon suppresses display of backbone atoms; use cartoon suppressBackbone false to see them.
Missing sidechain atoms (sel template-mismatch) can affect MLP/ESP calculations; dockprep #1 repairs them and adds hydrogens, but the tutorial says it makes little difference here.
hide /A hides only atoms; add targ acs to also hide cartoons and surfaces.
Coloring commands (color byattribute, mlp, coulombic) apply to models that already exist; open the protein first (#1) then the MOLE file (#2) so model numbers match the tutorial.

The page contains no old-Chimera notes; the MOLE JSON format, mlp, coulombic surfaces and color byattribute commands used here are ChimeraX-specific and have no direct equivalents on this page for old Chimera.
Open the tutorial with 'open <url>' inside ChimeraX: its cxcmd: links run commands only in the ChimeraX browser, not in a normal web browser.

Several commands can be typed on one line separated by semicolons; put a 'wait N' whose N matches the motion's frame count between the motion and 'movie encode' so the recording captures the whole motion.
Commands can be stored one per line in a plain-text .cxc file (e.g. on the Desktop) and run with 'open ~/Desktop/file.cxc'.

Toolbar icons are just commands: preset pub = set bg white + set silhouettes true; preset interactive = set bg black + set silhouettes false; view-all icon = view cofr false; hide/style icons act on selAtoms.
Model numbers are assumed in order: structure #1, density map #2 (or second structure #2), morph #3; adjust ids if your session differs.

The page's click-link for 'select far atoms' (sel zone :309 10 extend true) actually selects atoms near the galactose, so 'hide sel' after it hides the binding site; the intended step is a ctrl-drag box selection of the far atoms.
Recording in the Residue Fit tool is done with the tool's own record/stop buttons, not with commands.
The ChimeraX browser cannot handle download links; use a normal browser for the YouTube 360 Video Metadata app and YouTube upload.
A 360° VR video needs a 1:1 window aspect ratio and must have spherical + stereoscopic metadata injected before uploading to YouTube.
~/Desktop paths in movie encode expand to the home directory; movie1.mp4, movie2.mp4, movie3.mp4, resfit.mp4 and gbp.mp4 all land on the Desktop.
'ligand' is a built-in atom specifier; in 3gbp the galactose is residue :309.
The page contains only ChimeraX commands; its linked 'original' March 2017 version is also a ChimeraX tutorial, so no old-Chimera (1.x) edition can be derived from this source.
The tutorial targets ChimeraX 1.2 or newer; its command links execute directly when the page is opened inside ChimeraX via Help / Tutorials.

Toolbar buttons (Show Atoms, Hide Cartoon, H-bonds, etc.) act only on the current selection when one exists, otherwise on everything; clear the selection (ctrl-click background or 'select clear') to act on all.
Model numbers in the commands assume the tutorial's open order (e.g. atomic model #1, map #2, nanobody #3); check the Models panel and adjust ids.
Chain and ligand links in the Log panel are shortcuts for 'select' commands; ions like CL are hidden until you 'show' them.
Hydrogen atoms are present in 7kkj but not visible in density; use 'hide H' to reduce clutter when comparing to maps.
The up/down arrow keys broaden or narrow a selection (atom -> residue -> secondary structure -> chain).
Rainbow coloring runs N (blue) to C (red); beta sheets are not contiguous in sequence so strands of one sheet get different colors.
Molecular surfaces are per chain, solvent-excluded, and do not enclose waters or ligands.
Sequence Viewer residues with a black outline box have no atom coordinates (e.g. the C-terminal His tag).
The full EMD-22910 map is 226 MB; use the 7 MB trimmed file unless you have a fast (>100 Mbit/s) connection.
In the move-model mouse mode a residue or atom of the model must be selected so only that model moves; pressing or releasing Shift toggles between translating and rotating.
fitmap / fit is a local rigid optimization, so the model must be placed roughly by hand first; correctly orienting a small nanobody is very challenging.
Snapshot saves the on-screen size; use 'save file.png width N' for higher resolution and 'transparent true' when overlaying on other images.
Next step after rigid fitting would be flexible refinement with ISOLDE (no commands given on the page).
This page contains only ChimeraX commands and no legacy Chimera equivalents, so an old-Chimera edition cannot be derived from it without inventing commands.
In tomograms, lower map values correspond to higher density, so invert with volume scale factor -1 to make proteins appear bright.
volume scale creates a copy in memory and does not modify the original map, so close the original afterwards; model numbers then shift (scaled map #2, markers #1, boxed map #3).
The full EMDB 4191 tomogram is 240 MB; a 25 MB middle-third file is provided for faster download.
Marker placement uses the right mouse button (Cmd+click on Mac) after choosing the Plane button on the Markers toolbar.
Blob mouse mode reports lengths along the principal axes of inertia, and blob coloring is lost when the surface level is changed.
The record button on the volume morph slider saves the morph movie to the Desktop.
Guo's subtomogram average proteasome maps are half-proteasomes, so extra chains of the atomic model must be deleted before fitting.
fit (fitmap) only performs rigid rotation and translation from the current position, so place the model manually first with the Move Model mouse mode (shift to rotate, no shift to translate).
Several steps are GUI-only on the page (Volume Viewer plane style, yellow brightness curve, Plane slider, Move Model mouse mode); they have no explicit command in the tutorial.
The page contains ChimeraX commands only; no old-Chimera (Chimera 1.x) syntax appears on it, so an old-Chimera edition cannot be derived faithfully from this page.
The tutorial was written for ChimeraX 0.91 daily build (Sept 2019); command syntax is still valid but default model numbers, colors and log output may differ slightly in current versions.
Model numbers (#1, #2, #3) depend on the order things were opened; the cryoEM section assumes 6h6b is #1, 6rt0 is #2 and the EMDB map is #3, so check the Models panel before copying commands.
The page contains only ChimeraX commands; no legacy UCSF Chimera syntax is shown, so a faithful Chimera edition cannot be derived from it.
Only residues 38-95 of alpha-synuclein are in the 6h6b atomic model; the rest are disordered and not seen in the cryoEM map, so specs like :30 will match nothing.

In the sequence panel, black outline boxes mark residues absent from the atomic model and a blue background marks beta strands; selections are mirrored between the sequence panel and the 3D structure.
Ctrl-click a ribbon to select a residue, press up-arrow to extend the selection to the whole secondary-structure element, and ctrl-click the background to clear.
Several commands can be put on one line separated by a semicolon, e.g. 'surface close ; hide ribbon'.
'show surfaces' and 'mlp' have Molecule Display toolbar buttons that do the same thing.
mlp colors surfaces yellow for hydrophobic and blue for hydrophilic; hbonds draws dashed blue lines and ~hbonds removes them.
In cryoEM PDB entries the B-factor column often holds a local-resolution-like quantity rather than true B-factors; 'color bfactor' gives blue for best and red for worst.
The distance mouse mode in the toolbar (click two atoms) is an alternative to the 'distance' command; '~distance' removes all distance monitors.
'align ... reportMatrix true' prints the rotation angle and shift along the axis in the Log, which is how the fibril twist (179.5 degrees) and half-layer offset (2.45 A) were obtained.
matchmaker handles sequence differences by doing a sequence alignment first, so it can superimpose different polymorphs.
morph works on whole models, so delete all chains except the ones you want to morph first; 'delete #1 & ~/I,G' means delete model #1 except chains I and G.
Press the red circle button at the right of the morph slider to record the morph as a movie.
swapaa places the new side chain to avoid clashes or optimize hydrogen bonds, but molecular dynamics in other software may be needed afterward to relieve remaining clashes.
'volume region' takes grid indices imin,jmin,kmin,imax,jmax,kmax; the crop mouse mode is the interactive alternative for showing a thin slab.
At 3.1 A map resolution it can be difficult to position side chains correctly; disordered regions are averaged out of the 3D map.
The tutorial uses ChimeraX 1.10.1, except Scenes, which need a ChimeraX daily build from October 2025 or newer.
Scenes currently handle atomic models and maps but not molecular surfaces.
The morph command pairs chains by matching chain identifiers; wild motion of some chains means the superimposed chains do not share IDs, so rename them with changechains and recompute the morph.
Hover the mouse over chains to read their chain identifiers.
The morph slider has no loop option; use coordset with bounce true and loop N to play it repeatedly.
Simple lighting (light simple) makes morph playback faster than soft lighting.

When recording with movie record ... wait N ... movie encode, the wait frame count must cover the whole motion (e.g. 310 for a 51-frame morph bounced 3 times, 360 for a 360-frame roll, 600 for a 600-frame rock).
Movies are recorded at 25 frames per second, so wait 50 pauses for 2 seconds.
EMDB map 48725 is 75 MB compressed and can be slow to fetch; the tutorial provides a trimmed 22 MB version (data/trimmed_maps.zip) instead.
Morphing truncates the mutated residue R221E, so show the original 9my3 and 9my4 structures at the beginning and end of the movie.
Use movie crossfade to fade models in and out gradually between depiction changes.
Prepare a session with all colors, styles, labels and map zones first, then drive the movie from a .cxc command script.
Save a session containing the scenes so the movie can be re-recorded later with changes such as a black background or higher resolution.
The red circle button on the morph slider records a movie directly from the GUI.
Model numbering in the tutorial: 9my3 = #1, 9my4 = #2, morph = #3, active-state map = #4, intermediate-state map = #5.
A new animation timeline tool (menu Tools / General / Animations in daily builds) lets you drag scenes onto a timeline but does not yet do rolls, morphs or fades; expected in the Spring 2026 release.
Opening the tutorial HTML in ChimeraX (or via Help / Tutorials) makes its command links executable with a click.
Model numbers are assumed throughout the tutorial: map #1, PDB 7sth #2, AlphaFold model #3, PDB 7sl1 #4, morph #5; adapt specifiers if models were opened in a different order.

Almost every GUI step on the page has a command equivalent shown right after it (Models panel -> hide/show model, Molecule Display toolbar -> color bychain/surface/style, Actions/Color menu -> color sel, Tools/Volume Data/Surface Zone -> volume zone).
Large EMDB maps may open at a coarser step; 'volume #N step 1' shows the full resolution at the cost of speed.
The displayed command 'save irmap.png' actually runs 'save ~/Desktop/irmap.png' when clicked on the page; a bare filename saves to the current working directory.
Ctrl-click a ribbon then press the up-arrow key to expand the selection to the whole secondary-structure element; ctrl-click empty background clears the selection.
'volume zone ... near sel range 3' hides map outside 3 A of the selection; use 'volume unzone' to restore the full map before fitting or general viewing.
AlphaFold confidence coloring is blue = high, red = low; differently colored PAE domains have uncertain relative packing, so fit domains into the map individually.
Delete regions of a predicted model that are not in the map (e.g. the cytoplasmic kinase) before fitting.

fitmap performs a local rigid-body optimization, so first drag the model roughly into place with the 'translate selected models' mouse mode (right mouse; Mac: Option + trackpad drag; Shift to rotate).
Mouse-move modes act only on selected models, so select the model before dragging.
Before 'morph', roughly superimpose the second conformation on the first by hand; 'same true' requires identical residue/atom naming in both models.
Semicolons chain multiple commands on one line; 'wait 50' is used so movie recording captures the full morph playback before 'movie encode'.
The page contains ChimeraX commands only; no legacy Chimera command syntax appears anywhere, so a Chimera edition could not be derived from this source without inventing commands.
Command links on the tutorial page only execute inside ChimeraX when the page is opened via Help / Documentation Index > Tutorials; in an external browser they are plain text.
Model numbers in the tutorial (#1 model, #2 map, #3 x-ray, #4 morph or smoothed map) assume the exact open order; check the Model Panel and substitute the right ids in your own session.
Morphing and clip-plane dragging are much faster with atom (not cartoon) style and 'light simple'; switch to soft/full lighting only after positioning.
In morph, 'wrap true' returns to the starting conformation and 'same true' skips sequence alignment by assuming identical sequences (faster, but only valid for the same protein).
Large maps open subsampled; use 'volume #N step 1' to see full resolution.
Contour levels are map-specific: weak features such as a tentatively assigned phosphate may only appear at a lower level, so hand-adjust on the Volume Viewer histogram.
Mesh subdivision ('volume subdivide true', up to subdivisionlevels 2) looks finer but slows surface calculations; turn it off with 'vol #N subdivide false' when done.
Fine detail in a high-resolution map can prevent 'fit' from finding a global optimum; make a Gaussian-smoothed copy ('volume gaussian #N sdev 3') and fit into that for a larger radius of convergence.
Fitting will not choose between symmetry-related placements (e.g. 6-fold); the correct alignment of asymmetric parts must be set by hand.
Fit in Map needs a rough hand placement first: select the model, then use the 'translate selected models' / 'rotate selected models' right-mouse modes.
Ctrl-click a ribbon selects one residue; pressing the up-arrow key expands the selection to the whole chain.
In clip mouse mode, hold the alt key to move the far (back) clip plane, and click without dragging to turn clipping off.
Wildcard chain specs such as '/c*' match all chains whose IDs start with that letter (c0..c9 here).
On a Mac trackpad: 2-finger rotate, 3-finger translate, 4-finger (or pinch) zoom; disable 3-finger Mission Control in System Preferences > Trackpad > More Gestures.
Center of rotation is on the surface when zoomed in close and at the model center when zoomed out.

This page contains only ChimeraX syntax; an old-Chimera edition cannot be derived from it (commands such as morph, preset, volume subdivide, color zone and mousemode have different or no equivalents there), so that would need a separate Chimera source.
The tutorial was tested on ChimeraX 1.9 and is written for Mac path conventions; it contains no legacy Chimera syntax, so no old-Chimera edition can be derived from this page.
Every GUI action prints its equivalent command in the Log; copy those lines into a .cxc file to make any workflow reproducible.
Set a working folder with 'cd' (or File > Set Working Folder) so save/open commands need no full paths.
Multiple commands can be typed on one line separated by semicolons.
Many commands and keywords accept short forms: tr = transparency, c = cartoon, a = atoms, s = surface, mm = matchmaker.
ChimeraX does not auto-save and never asks for confirmation before closing models or quitting.
In movie scripts add a 'wait' after every step, otherwise the next command runs while the previous one is still animating.
Named views are stored in the session but cannot be moved between sessions; use 'view matrix' to capture coordinates for reuse.
'name frozen X sel' pins a name to the currently selected items; names without 'frozen' are dynamic and apply to models opened later too.
The 'last-opened' model specifier avoids knowing model numbers in scripts; alternatively give an explicit unlikely id such as 'open 7ZNJ id 1000'.
'alphafold interfaces' on an AF3 folder is currently limited to dimeric predictions and reports in the Log rather than changing the display.
AlphaMissense scores exist only for human proteins; folded domains tend to light up entirely while hits in disordered regions often mark contact motifs.
Every newly opened structure gets the default display style; re-apply presets after loading.
'mcopy #A to #B' copies all style attributes (colors, representation) from one model to another.
The '~' prefix negates a command or spec: '~label ~interface' removes labels from everything outside the named selection.
Chain-description selectors like //description='*THO complex subunit 4' find all copies of a protein without knowing chain IDs.
The ChimeraX BLAST tool cannot restrict to a single species; use the Similar Structures tool for fast structure-based search of the whole AlphaFold database.
If you forget syntax, type the command without arguments and click it in the Log to open the help; 'alias list' shows all aliases, and an alias with 'echo' just prints a reminder.
Use 'name list builtins true' to see all built-in selection groups.
Arrow keys broaden (up), narrow (down) or invert (left/right; shift for all models) the current selection; hovering over a residue shows its identifier.
In Preferences > Window, enable 'Resize graphics window on session restore' for consistent figure sizes across sessions.
The Toolshed (Tools > More Tools) provides extensions such as ISOLDE, ArtiaX, XMAS and the CliX autocompleting command line.

As of ChimeraX 1.13 the DICOM/medical-image features (Download DICOM, DICOM Browser, Segmentations, etc.) are no longer bundled and must be installed as the MedicalImaging bundle from the ChimeraX Toolshed.
The tutorial's click-to-execute links only work when the page is viewed in the ChimeraX Browser (open its URL with the open command).
Download DICOM shows a one-time TCIA terms-of-use disclaimer and then caches dataset info so it starts faster next time.
'Download and Open' in the Download DICOM tool is a blocking operation: ChimeraX freezes until the download finishes and the data opens.
RIDER Lung CT is the recommended TCIA dataset for this tutorial; other datasets may cause problems (file a bug report or email chimerax-users).
When new DICOM data is opened, ChimeraX merges it into any already-open matching patient, study, or series model, and the DICOM Browser updates automatically.
Selecting a Patient or Study in the Model Panel and clicking 'Info' opens the DICOM Browser, but selecting a series opens the per-file DICOM Metadata tool instead.
Before 'segmentations create', look up the DICOM image's model number (e.g. #1.1.1) in the Model Panel or Volume Viewer; the new segmentation gets its own model number (e.g. #2).
Clicking a 2D slice with no segmentation present creates one automatically.
Opening the Segmentations tool switches the 3D view to surface style and adds the 2D slices to the Volume Viewer, where they can be windowed and leveled independently of the 3D model.
Use the arrow keys (SHIFT+arrow for ten slices) or the slice slider to move through slices when a 2D view is in focus.

All views share the same segmentation data, so changing a segmentation's opacity in the Volume Viewer affects every view; the factory default opacity is 80% and can be changed in the tool's options menu.
While adding to or removing from a segmentation in 3D, ChimeraX renders it at slightly lower resolution for speed and restores full resolution when the operation stops.
Closing the Segmentations tool or closing all models automatically resets the mouse modes; closing all models also closes the tool and resets the view to the default 3D-only layout.
Segmentations can be saved to disk in DICOM format and are re-associated with their source patient and study when next opened (the tutorial gives no explicit save command).

The tutorial (May 2024) uses 'segmentations setMouseModes' / 'segmentations resetMouseModes', while the current command reference documents 'segmentations mouseModes on|off' and 'segmentations handModes on|off'; try the reference form if the tutorial form is not recognized.
In VR, other controller buttons keep their defaults: left trigger, left grip, or right trigger still move the reference data, and the Y button summons the ChimeraX UI.

Old-Chimera note (not from the page): every feature in this tutorial (Download DICOM/TCIA, DICOM Browser, DICOM Metadata, Segmentations tool, ui view layouts, segmentations command, VR hand modes) is ChimeraX-only with no command-level equivalent in legacy Chimera, so an old-Chimera edition of this tutorial is not feasible.
The page is a reveal.js shell; the actual slides are at .../chimerax-comp-structures/module.html, and every command is embedded as a cxcmd: link.
Default label height is 0.7 Angstroms; use 'label height N' to change it.
'@@display' in an atom spec refers to the atom-level 'display' attribute, so 'label @@display' labels residues that have displayed atoms.

Dashed lines for non-covalent interactions are pseudobonds: purple = metal coordination, yellow = distances, light blue = H-bonds, bright purple = clashes; remove them with ~distance, ~hbonds, ~contacts, ~clashes.
Hover the cursor over an atom, bond or pseudobond in the graphics window to see a balloon with identity and length.

'sel restrict cross' in hbonds/contacts/clashes finds interactions with exactly one end in the selection; 'reveal t' displays partner atoms, 'log t' writes details to the Log, 'select t' selects the interacting atoms.
Clashes are unfavorable too-close contacts; contacts are all direct interactions (polar, nonpolar, favorable, unfavorable) including clashes, listed in the Log by decreasing VDW overlap.
Ctrl-click picks an atom; the up arrow key promotes the selection to the whole residue (press twice if a bond was picked).
'torsion' with four atoms only reports the angle; adding a value after the atoms sets it.

Rotamer probabilities in the Rotamers tool depend only on the residue's backbone phi/psi, not on interactions with the rest of the structure; use the dialog's H-Bonds and Clashes options to evaluate them in context.
'mouse right bond' assigns bond rotation to the right mouse button (trackpad + Alt on Windows, trackpad + Command on Mac).
'mlp' both creates the molecular surface and colors it: dark cyan hydrophilic, white, dark goldenrod lipophilic.
'color byattribute bfactor' maps blue (low) to red (high) by default; 'palette' and 'range' options change the mapping, and residue or model attributes can also be used.
After 'preset original' with two models, the first is tan and the second sky blue; check the Model Panel to see model numbers and colors.
'mm' is short for 'matchmaker'; clicking a light orange box in the sequence alignment selects the residue pairs used in the final fit (the common core).
Multiple commands can be combined on one line separated by semicolons, e.g. '~hbonds; ~clashes'.
A morph only includes atoms present in both input structures, so a ligand present in one structure is excluded; re-show it from the original model with 'show #1 models' and 'show #1:fps,mg'.
To record a whole morph trajectory as a movie from the slider interface, move the slider back to the beginning first.
